answers.label: Q.1
answers.solution:
Pure alcohol in 400 ml of a 15% solution \(= \frac{15}{100} \times 400 = 60\) ml
Let \(x\) ml of pure alcohol be added. Alcohol becomes \((60 + x)\) ml in \((400 + x)\) ml of solution.
\(\frac{60 + x}{400 + x} = \frac{32}{100}\)
\(100(60 + x) = 32(400 + x)\)
\(6000 + 100x = 12800 + 32x\)
\(68x = 6800\)
\(x = 100\)
Check: 160 ml of alcohol in 500 ml is \(\frac{160}{500} = 32\%\).
So, 100 ml of pure alcohol must be added.

Let the number of 10 paise coins be \(x\).
Number of 25 paise coins \(= 3x\)
Number of 50 paise coins \(= 3x + 5\)
Total value in paise: Rs 120 = 12000 paise.
\(10x + 25(3x) + 50(3x + 5) = 12000\)
\(10x + 75x + 150x + 250 = 12000\)
\(235x = 11750\)
\(x = 50\)
Check: 50 coins of 10 p = Rs 5, 150 coins of 25 p = Rs 37.50, 155 coins of 50 p = Rs 77.50; total Rs 120.
So, there are 50 coins of 10 paise.

He charges the cost price of 1000 g but gives only 950 g.
So on goods costing him the price of 950 g he receives the price of 1000 g.
Gain \(= 1000 - 950 = 50\) g worth
Gain % \(= \frac{50}{950} \times 100 = \frac{100}{19} = 5\frac{5}{19}\%\)
So, his gain is \(5\frac{5}{19}\%\) (about 5.26%).

answers.label: Q.5
answers.solution:
Numerator: \(x^{m+n} \times x^{n+l} \times x^{l+m} = x^{(m+n)+(n+l)+(l+m)} = x^{2(l+m+n)}\)
Denominator: \(x^m \times x^n \times x^l = x^{l+m+n}\)
Dividing: \(\frac{x^{2(l+m+n)}}{x^{l+m+n}} = x^{2(l+m+n) - (l+m+n)} = x^{l+m+n}\)
So, the expression simplifies to \(x^{l+m+n}\).

The four arcs have equal radii and meet at the midpoints of the sides, so each radius \(= \frac{14}{2} = 7\) cm.
Each arc is centred at a corner of the square, where the angle is \(90^\circ\), so each arc is a quarter circle.

Second part: \(2\sqrt{3}(4 \times 3\sqrt{3} - 5 \times 4\sqrt{3}) = 2\sqrt{3}(12\sqrt{3} - 20\sqrt{3}) = 2\sqrt{3} \times (-8\sqrt{3}) = -48\)

At the bottom left, the exterior angle is \(125^\circ\), so the angle the left side makes with line BC (inside the figure) is \(180^\circ - 125^\circ = 55^\circ\).
At D, the angle between DE and the right side is \(112^\circ\), so the right side makes \(180^\circ - 112^\circ = 68^\circ\) with the line DE on the other side.
Draw a line through the top vertex parallel to BC and DE.
By alternate angles, the left side makes \(55^\circ\) with this line, and the right side makes \(68^\circ\) with it.
These two angles and x together form a straight angle at the top vertex:
\(x = 180^\circ - 55^\circ - 68^\circ = 57^\circ\)
So, \(x = 57^\circ\).

125-130: 1, 130-135: 2, 135-140: 3, 140-145: 7, 145-150: 4, 150-155: 2, 155-160: 1.

(i) The graph shows the number of girls of Class X in different height groups (heights in cm, in intervals of 5 cm).
(ii) The tallest bar is 140-145 cm, with 7 girls.
(iii) Girls with height 140 cm and above \(= 7 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 14\). Percentage \(= \frac{14}{20} \times 100 = 70\%\).

answers.label: Q.11
answers.solution:
The four lines form a quadrilateral in the middle, and a small triangle at each of its four corners.
In each triangle, the angle at the quadrilateral's corner is vertically opposite to an interior angle of the quadrilateral.
In the four triangles:
\(p + q + A = 180^\circ\), \(r + s + B = 180^\circ\), \(t + u + C = 180^\circ\), \(v + w + D = 180^\circ\)
where A, B, C, D are the interior angles of the quadrilateral.
Adding: \((p + q + r + s + t + u + v + w) + (A + B + C + D) = 720^\circ\)
The angles of a quadrilateral add up to \(360^\circ\), so
\(p + q + r + s + t + u + v + w = 720^\circ - 360^\circ = 360^\circ\)
So, the sum is \(360^\circ\).

Cost of 35 kg at Rs 4.50 \(= 35 \times 4.50 = \text{Rs } 157.50\)
Total cost of 60 kg \(= 100 + 157.50 = \text{Rs } 257.50\)
Selling price of 60 kg at Rs 4.50 \(= 60 \times 4.50 = \text{Rs } 270\)
Profit \(= 270 - 257.50 = \text{Rs } 12.50\)
So, Hariram makes a profit of Rs 12.50.

The largest four digit number is 9999.
\(86 \times 116 = 9976\) and \(86 \times 117 = 10062\) (five digits).
So \(9999 = 86 \times 116 + 23\); the remainder is 23.
Required number \(= 9999 - 23 = 9976\)
So, the largest four digit number divisible by 86 is 9976.

LCM of 6, 9 and 7 is 126.
\(\frac{1}{6} + \frac{4}{9} + \frac{2}{7} = \frac{21}{126} + \frac{56}{126} + \frac{36}{126} = \frac{113}{126}\)
The additive inverse of a number is the number which added to it gives 0.
So, the additive inverse is \(-\frac{113}{126}\).

Area of trapezium \(= \frac{1}{2} \times (\text{sum of parallel sides}) \times \text{height}\)
\(306 = \frac{1}{2} \times (7x + 11x) \times 17\)
\(306 = 9x \times 17 = 153x\)
\(x = 2\)
Parallel sides \(= 7 \times 2 = 14\) cm and \(11 \times 2 = 22\) cm.
So, the parallel sides are 14 cm and 22 cm.

Total cost of 3 fans \(= 3 \times 450 = \text{Rs } 1350\)
For a 20% gain on the whole, total selling price \(= \frac{120}{100} \times 1350 = \text{Rs } 1620\)
One fan sold at 10% loss: SP \(= \frac{90}{100} \times 450 = \text{Rs } 405\)
SP needed for the other two \(= 1620 - 405 = \text{Rs } 1215\)
Each of them \(= \frac{1215}{2} = \text{Rs } 607.50\)
So, the other two fans must be sold for Rs 1215 in all, that is Rs 607.50 each.

The marked \(120^\circ\) is at the point where line f meets line a: between f (going up towards the top point) and a (going right).
Angles on a straight line: the angle between a (going right) and f (going down) \(= 180^\circ - 120^\circ = 60^\circ\).
x: at the top left corner, between a and c. Since c is parallel to f, x is the corresponding angle to this \(60^\circ\), so \(x = 60^\circ\).
y: where c meets d (bottom line), between d (going left) and c (going down). Since a is parallel to d and c is parallel to f, this angle matches the \(120^\circ\) angle (both lines turned through half a turn), so \(y = 120^\circ\). (Check: the angle between d going right and c going down is \(60^\circ\), and \(180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ\).)
z: at the bottom right corner, between d (going left) and f (going up). These are alternate angles to the \(60^\circ\) angle between a and f (a parallel to d), so \(z = 60^\circ\).
In the same way every point of the star is \(60^\circ\) and every angle inside the hexagon is \(120^\circ\).
So, \(x = 60^\circ\), \(y = 120^\circ\), \(z = 60^\circ\).

\(\left(\frac{x^m}{x^n}\right)^l = x^{(m-n)l} = x^{lm - ln}\)
\(\left(\frac{x^n}{x^l}\right)^m = x^{(n-l)m} = x^{mn - lm}\)
\(\left(\frac{x^l}{x^m}\right)^n = x^{(l-m)n} = x^{ln - mn}\)
Product \(= x^{(lm - ln) + (mn - lm) + (ln - mn)} = x^0 = 1\)
So, the value is 1.

Let the length of the train be \(L\) m. To pass a bridge, the train covers (its length + the bridge's length).
Speed \(= \frac{L + 300}{15} = \frac{L + 450}{21}\)
\(21(L + 300) = 15(L + 450)\)
\(21L + 6300 = 15L + 6750\)
\(6L = 450\)
\(L = 75\) m
Speed \(= \frac{75 + 300}{15} = \frac{375}{15} = 25\) m/s
In km/hr: \(25 \times \frac{18}{5} = 90\) km/hr
Check: \(\frac{75 + 450}{21} = \frac{525}{21} = 25\) m/s.
So, the speed is 90 km/hr and the length of the train is 75 m.

\(2x + 4 = 4(x - 6)\)
\(2x + 4 = 4x - 24\)
\(2x = 28\)
\(x = 14\)

Check: \(28 + 4 = 32 = 4 \times (14 - 6)\).
Two years ago: Shyam \(14 - 2 = 12\) years, Karthik \(28 - 2 = 26\) years.
So, two years ago Shyam was 12 and Karthik was 26.

answers.solution:
2 men do the same work as 3 women, so 1 man \(= \frac{3}{2}\) women.
4 men \(= 4 \times \frac{3}{2} = 6\) women.
4 men and 9 women \(= 6 + 9 = 15\) women.
3 women take 40 hours, so the work is \(3 \times 40 = 120\) woman-hours.
Time for 15 women \(= \frac{120}{15} = 8\) hours
So, 4 men and 9 women will finish the work in 8 hours.

The figure is a rectangle 28 cm by 14 cm. The unshaded semicircle stands on the 14 cm side, so its radius \(r = 7\) cm.
Area of rectangle \(= 28 \times 14 = 392\) cm\(^2\)
Area of semicircle \(= \frac{1}{2}\pi r^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 = 77\) cm\(^2\)
Shaded area \(= 392 - 77 = 315\) cm\(^2\)
The shaded region is bounded by the top side, the right side, the bottom side and the curved edge of the semicircle (the 14 cm left side is not part of it).
Length of the semicircular arc \(= \pi r = \frac{22}{7} \times 7 = 22\) cm
Perimeter \(= 28 + 14 + 28 + 22 = 92\) cm
So, the shaded area is 315 cm\(^2\) and its perimeter is 92 cm.

Let the polygons have \(n\) and \(2n\) sides.
Interior angle of a regular polygon with \(n\) sides \(= \frac{(n - 2) \times 180^\circ}{n}\)
First: \(\frac{(n - 2) \times 180^\circ}{n}\); second: \(\frac{(2n - 2) \times 180^\circ}{2n} = \frac{(n - 1) \times 180^\circ}{n}\)
Their ratio is \(3 : 4\):
\(\frac{n - 2}{n - 1} = \frac{3}{4}\)
\(4(n - 2) = 3(n - 1)\)
\(4n - 8 = 3n - 3\)
\(n = 5\)
Check: pentagon \(108^\circ\), decagon \(144^\circ\), and \(108 : 144 = 3 : 4\).
So, the polygons have 5 and 10 sides.
